## Fixed Issues

### CR-01: Tailwind compiles a planning document into invalid CSS; every route 500s

**Files modified:** `app/globals.css`, `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css`
**Commit:** `29480f9`

Applied the reviewer's preferred, fail-closed form:

```css
@import "tailwindcss" source(none);

@source "./";              /* app/ */
@source "../components";
@source "../lib";
@source "../actions";
```

The `@source not` alternative was **deliberately not used**, per the review's
own argument — it fails open, and the next documentation directory anyone adds
is scanned by default with nobody remembering to come back. A ~30-line comment
above the allowlist records the outage, why bare `@source` would not have
prevented it (it is additive in v4), and the rule that adding a directory here
means adding it to `SCANNED_DIRS` in both gates.

`.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css` got the same treatment: because it imports
`../app/globals.css`, it now inherits `source(none)`, so its four previously-
additive `@source` lines became a real scope. `../actions` was added for parity
with the app, and a comment records that `./previews` is deliberately extra
there and must never migrate into `globals.css` — the preview cards ship
nothing to diners, and their utilities inflating the app sheet is the DINE-03
payload regression that entry exists to keep out.

Confirmed neither `shadcn/tailwind.css` nor `tw-animate-css` declares its own
`@source`, so nothing re-opened detection from a dependency.

**Commit `3fab16a`** then did the "and only then" half — the prose:

- `01.1-10-SUMMARY.md:28` — the `...` shorthand replaced with the real property
  name (`--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height`), which is what
  `venue-switcher-menu.tsx:113` actually ships, plus a note telling the next
  editor not to re-elide it and why.
- `01.1-05-SUMMARY.md:213` — `rounded-[…]` de-bracketed to `rounded-…`. It was
  an elision already, so nothing is lost and it stops being a candidate.
- `01.1-05-SUMMARY.md:219` — `text-[0.8rem]` rewritten as prose.

This half is now defense-in-depth rather than the fix, which is the ordering
the review asked for.

### CR-02: The compiler's input is broader than every gate that polices it

**Files modified:** `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts`, `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts`
**Commit:** `69c865b`

Added GROUP 5, four assertions that pin the premise the rest of the gate rests
on. **One deliberate strengthening of the reviewer's proposal:** the review's
snippet hardcodes `new Set(["./", "../components", "../lib", "../actions"])`.
Hardcoding lets someone widen `SCANNED_DIRS` to silence a failing scan without
the CSS noticing, or widen the CSS without the scan noticing — the same drift
one level up. The expectation is instead **derived** from `SCANNED_DIRS`:

```ts
const EXPECTED_SOURCE_ARGUMENTS = new Set(
  SCANNED_DIRS.map((dir) => (dir === "app" ? "./" : `../${dir}`)),
);
```

so the two sets are equal by construction and the only way to change what
Tailwind compiles is to change what the gate polices, in the same edit.

For that equality to be true rather than approximate, `"actions"` was added to
`SCANNED_DIRS` in **both** gates — the review noted they scan three directories
while the compiler consumes four. Both suites stay green with the wider scope.

A fourth assertion bans `@source not` outright, so the fail-open form cannot be
introduced later as a "simpler" repair.

### WR-02: `select.tsx` and `tooltip.tsx` animate through `prefers-reduced-motion`

**Files modified:** `components/ui/select.tsx`, `components/ui/tooltip.tsx`, `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts`
**Commit:** `b2a0fcc`

`select.tsx` — `duration-100` replaced with `duration-(--duration-base)`, plus
`motion-reduce:animate-none`. `tooltip.tsx` — both added (it declared no
duration at all).

Then made it enforceable, as the review asked, with GROUP 4b. Three assertions
rather than the one proposed: the offender scan, a non-vacuity guard pinning
the animated-primitive count at 4 (so a utility rename cannot silently empty
the set), and a **third check the review did not specify** — that no animated
primitive hardcodes `duration-<number>`. That third one matters because it is
the half `motion-reduce:animate-none` does not cover: `duration-100` is immune
to the token override regardless of whether the animation is gated, which is
precisely how `select.tsx` opted out.

Verified in the compiled CSS that both `motion-reduce:animate-none` and
`motion-reduce:transition-none` emit real `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)`
rules.

### WR-03: `button.tsx` uses `transition-all` on a transform

**File modified:** `components/ui/button.tsx`
**Commit:** `285e26a`

Replaced `transition-all` with the review's explicit-property alternative
rather than its `transition-colors` suggestion, because **`transition-colors`
omits `box-shadow`** and the focus ring three declarations along
(`focus-visible:ring-3`) is a box-shadow. The property list used is exactly
`--transition-control`'s:

```
transition-[color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow]
duration-(--duration-base) ease-(--ease-out-soft) motion-reduce:transition-none
```

Taking duration and easing from the tokens is what makes the
`prefers-reduced-motion` override at `primitives.css:111-116` reach this file
at all — that override works by zeroing `--duration-base`, and Tailwind's
default duration is immune to it. Side effect: this retires `--ease-out-soft`
from IN-02's dead-token list.

Verified in the compiled output:
`transition-property:color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow`,
`.duration-\(--duration-base\){--tw-duration:var(--duration-base)}`,
`.ease-\(--ease-out-soft\){--tw-ease:var(--ease-out-soft)}`.

The `active:...:translate-y-px` press offset now snaps instead of easing in
over 150ms, which is the contract's intent.

### WR-04: `<html lang="en">` hardcoded in a three-language product

**File modified:** `app/layout.tsx`
**Commit:** `1358873`

Took the review's "minimum viable for this phase" — record the constraint — and
this one is **flagged for a Phase 2 decision rather than solved**. The reason is
structural and worth stating: only a root layout may render `<html>`, so the
diner group *cannot* override `lang` in a nested layout. The real fix is either
splitting into multiple root layouts (delete `app/layout.tsx`; give each
top-level group its own `<html>`/`<body>`) or lifting the value out of the
literal — an architectural change owned by the phase that ships the
multilingual surface, not by a review-fix pass.

The comment names both options, the WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.1 failure, and the concrete
harm (Romanian/Hungarian allergen names announced with English phonemes, on the
surface CLAUDE.md makes legally load-bearing). **The review also asks for a
corresponding row in the Phase 2 plan; that is a planning artifact this agent
does not own — see § Handoff.**

### WR-05: Supabase error channels discarded in three reads

**Files modified:** `app/(tablet)/enable-staff-mode/page.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx`
**Commit:** `a76e3b7`

(b) and (c) in `enable-staff-mode/page.tsx` now bind `error` and throw, exactly
as the review specifies.

(a) `VenueSwitcher.tsx` was fixed **differently from (b) and (c), on purpose.**
The review says (a) "should follow for consistency"; copying the throw there
would have been worse than the defect. `VenueSwitcher` is rendered *by* the
dashboard layout, and a React error boundary does not catch errors thrown in
the layout that declares it — so a throw would sail past
`app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` and replace the entire application shell with the
global error page, trading every dashboard screen for a transient fault in a
piece of chrome. The channel is therefore **bound and then deliberately not
thrown**: the error case is now its own branch, logged server-side with code and
message, and the comment argues the exception rather than leaving it to look
like the original oversight. The "no list, no switcher" conflation the review
objected to is gone either way.

### WR-06: `EnableStaffModeForm` renders an unsubmittable form on zero venues

**File modified:** `app/(tablet)/components/EnableStaffModeForm.tsx`
**Commit:** `dd73c45`

Explicit `venues.length === 0` branch returning a destructive `Alert` with
`COPY.errors.readFailed`, placed before `singleVenue` is computed. The comment
records why the check cannot be delegated to the page above: `.in("id", ids)`
can return fewer rows than ids when RLS filters them, so `ownedVenueIds.length`
and `venues.length` are genuinely different numbers.

**Files modified:** `.../staff/components/deactivate-staff-dialog.tsx`, `.../staff/devices/components/revoke-device-dialog.tsx`
**Commit:** `5665268`

All three exits gated in both dialogs: `onOpenChange` guarded on `pending`

**File modified:** `app/(tablet)/components/NameGridPinPad.tsx`
**Commit:** `04aaf37`

All three sub-defects: `startHold` clears before arming; a `useEffect` cleanup
clears on unmount (the success branch replaces the render tree on every PIN

### WR-09: `FieldError` de-duplicates on a possibly-undefined key

**File modified:** `components/ui/field.tsx`
**Commit:** `38eafa2`

Rewritten to filter message-less errors out *first*, then de-duplicate on the
message string via a `Set`, with an explicit `length === 0 → return null`. This
closes all three defects at once — the `==`, the meaningless optional chain,
and the `undefined`-key collapse that produced an empty `<ul>` inside a
`role="alert"` element. The list now keys on the message rather than the array
index. Confirmed by grep that no loose equality remains in the file.
